transcript.note: Round 1, built lattice-first per this chain's criterion order rather than from any pre-existing layout. (1) Interchanges first: of the 26 deg>=3 nodes, the eleven that carry the downtown are placed as an explicit 3x4 grid of trunk intersections, because winding order is only defined at these points and settling them settles the only thing that can reject the batch. Three vertical trunks — Tamsui-Xinyi at col 35 (gx 743-762), Zhonghe-Xinlu at col 42 (gx 778-788), Wenhu at col 45 (gx 814-851) — cross four horizontal trunks — Tamsui-Xinyi's east arm at row 25 (gy 624-640), Bannan at row 27 (gy 583-611), Songshan-Xindian's east arm at row 31 (gy 566-579), and the Airport/Xinlu west chain at row 34 (gy 526-556). Every intersection is a real interchange: 23/12/22 on row 25, 44/40/17 on row 27, 24/10/30 on row 31, 25/9 on row 34. The trunk order matches geography on both axes (750<783<814 west-to-east, 362<394<428<462 south-to-north). (2) One line, one direction: with the lattice fixed, each remaining line was given a single axis and its classified nodes threaded along it — Bannan runs 36-44-40-17-34 straight across row 27, Songshan-Xindian 58-24-10-30-41 straight across row 31, and the Airport line plus the Xinlu west arm 7-11-15-16-39-25-9 straight across row 34, seven stations in one line spanning the whole map. Column 20 carries Circular/Bannan 35-45-33-15 and, further north, Tamsui-Xinyi/Danhai 28-51-50; column 44 carries Songshan-Xindian's Xindian arm 21-6-13; column 0 carries the Airport line's far west 7-48-14; column 7 carries the Sanying stub 47-8. (3) Global relative position, which I had to check myself since this chain prints no orderFlip or meanDrift: I derived every column from the gx rank order and every row from the gy rank order, collapsing a group to a shared col/row only where the members are near-coincident, then verified the finished table both ways — sorting all 59 verts by gx yields non-decreasing columns and sorting by gy yields non-decreasing rows, with no strict inversion anywhere. (4) Squeeze and loosen: the interchange knot is packed into cols 31-45 x rows 23-34 while the outer branches (Sanying, Danhai, Ankeng, Airport west) are compressed onto single axes — those corners hold no other vertices, so compressing them cannot put anything on the wrong side of anything. Two snaps I refused on criterion-3 grounds: levelling 29 Tamsui onto 51 Hongshulin's row, and lifting 55 Nangang Exhibition onto Bannan's row, would each have bought an H segment but would have misplaced points that differ by 5-10% of the map's latitude. (5) All 59 cells are distinct, and every shared col/row carries only consecutive vertices of a single route, so no vertex should land inside a foreign edge.
